audit.corrected: Rows 1,2,3,5,6 moved to Fizz with matching whys; rows 0 and 4 already agreed. win[] already correct — side+why edits only.

edits.before: E online: the root that defines the lane. Land it and the Q follow-up chunks; miss it and you farm for fourteen seconds.
edits.after: His Urchin Strike trades hit through your slow answer, and Nimble Fighter blunts your Q. Hold E — thrown early, he hops it.

edits.before: W completes the setup: vision + slow from across the map. Root-into-W never misses, and the passive soul fragments heal you.
edits.after: Playful / Trickster online: he can dodge your E and Q on reaction while untargetable. Bait the hop or do not commit at all.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-spam stops costing the lane. Poke the wave contact and pull every rooted target with the passive.
edits.after: His 16s E is up for nearly every trade you attempt — you land Nevermove only off his mistakes. Farm with Q and hold the root.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: the drain outpaces their damage in any extended fight. Force rivers, root the entry, ascend, profit.
edits.after: His Rocketbelt/Lich Bane one-combo bursts you through Ascension, then he E's out of the root. Zhonya's before you duel him.

edits.before: Late Swain is the anti-team: flank-root their engage, ascend in their backline, and demonflare the clump that forms around you.
edits.after: Late he dodges your flank-root with the hop and leaves before the drain matters — peel by pre-rooting his jump, never chase.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Nevermove has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — a 16s cooldown at rank 1, 8s at max. The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo: bait it before your burst. - Chum the Waters is 120s at rank 1 — with the shark spent, his all-in loses its guaranteed opener.

edits.before: Brawling pre-6 like the demon is already online — Swain without R is a slow mage with a dream and a root on cooldown.
edits.after: His W bleed and auto-reset make chasing a losing trade — the wind-up is your cue to step back before the E hop punishes you.

edits.before: E his step-up, passive-pull the root for the chunk + heal, Q the retreat — every landed root is a won trade with a health refund attached.
edits.after: When he shoves and drops from vision, Vision of Empire on the river path buys the side lanes time — the reveal beats a roamer who arrives unseen.

notes: Packet defect: 'Swain wins 52.07% but the chart gives Fizz 7/7 stages'. I aligned the full layer to the content+packet chart (all Fizz) because the kit supports it — Fizz's untargetable E counters Swain's entire E-dependent pattern — and the WR tension is plausibly explained by Swain's teamfight scaling; if the user wants the chart softened toward the win rate, that is a data-owner call, not a kit call. Rows 0 and 4 already agreed. Fizz R is a blockable projectile that grounds and knocks up — Swain has no dash and no unstoppable, so only the sidestep advice (already in content) applies.
